2cffcdf9-9d32-4774-819f-e13d4ea05408.original_title: 97-year-old veteran finally receives medals after more than seven decades
2cffcdf9-9d32-4774-819f-e13d4ea05408.original_summary: A family celebration in Hawaii brings long-awaited recognition to a 97-year-old veteran whose military records were lost in a fire.
2cffcdf9-9d32-4774-819f-e13d4ea05408.original_body:
On November 21, 2026, Lorito Lastimado Acosta received military decorations at a surprise family ceremony in Honolulu. Acosta, 97, had served in the United States Army during World War II and the Korean War. A 1973 fire at the National Personnel Records Center had destroyed millions of records, including his. His discharge records established his eligibility for the awards, and family members and veteran groups helped arrange the ceremony. His family thanked attendees for bringing long-delayed recognition to a person who had spent decades supporting his loved ones.

b2ee5b88-bd3a-4864-95cd-fce4436b4dcf.original_title: Scientists crack a shipwreck lock’s code after more than 400 years
b2ee5b88-bd3a-4864-95cd-fce4436b4dcf.original_summary: A metal detectorist’s discovery led museum experts and Cardiff University researchers to unlock a Tudor-era brass padlock without damaging it.
b2ee5b88-bd3a-4864-95cd-fce4436b4dcf.original_body:
On 4 November 2026, Cardiff University and Museum Wales announced that researchers had worked out the combination of a brass lock recovered from the wreck of the Ann Francis, which sank off the Welsh coast in 1583.

Detectorist Peter Hughes had recovered artefacts from the wreck site over many years. Although he could turn the lock’s lettered rings, he did not know their correct positions. Researchers used micro-CT scans to examine the hidden mechanism without taking it apart. The museum team tested the sequence ANCE and successfully opened the lock.

The purpose of the lock is uncertain: it may have secured a chest or other container. The discovery is now part of the Ann Francis display at the National Waterfront Museum in Swansea.

Comparison image: a different copper-alloy combination lock dating from around 1550–1650, documented by the Portable Antiquities Scheme. It illustrates the historic type of mechanism, not the actual shipwreck artefact.

c6d9be0d-12ca-419e-8683-12e5e243d3a0.original_title: Thirteen rescued Barbary macaques return to the wild in Morocco
c6d9be0d-12ca-419e-8683-12e5e243d3a0.original_summary: A second group of macaques rescued from illegal trade and poaching has been released in Tazekka National Park.
c6d9be0d-12ca-419e-8683-12e5e243d3a0.original_body:
Stichting AAP reported on 7 May that 13 Barbary macaques had been released into Tazekka National Park. The group comprised eight adults, three juveniles and two young animals. The macaques had been confiscated by Moroccan authorities. On release, they climbed into the trees. Researchers are monitoring them with GPS collars to assess their adjustment and the prospects for a lasting wild population. The release follows an earlier group returned in October 2025.

eea11e7f-6000-48e9-ab70-49116ececcc2.summary: وتبين الملاحظات الجديدة التي أبدتها وكالة الفضاء الأوروبية بشأن الديموروفوس كيف أن اصطدام المركبة الفضائية المتعمد قد غير الكويكب، مما أدى إلى تعزيز البحوث المتعلقة بالدفاع الكوكبي.
eea11e7f-6000-48e9-ab70-49116ececcc2.body:
وفي 25 تشرين الثاني/نوفمبر 2026، قدمت وكالة الفضاء الأوروبية ملاحظات جديدة من بعثتها في هيرا. وتقوم المركبة الفضائية حاليا بفحص ديمورفوس، وهو الكويكب الصغير الذي تغيرت مداره عمدا عن طريق بعثة الوكالة الألمانية للتعاون التقني في أيلول/سبتمبر ٢٠٢٢.

وتكشف الملاحظات الجديدة عن حفرة تمتد إلى الجانب المتأثر. ووجد (هيرا) أيضاً أن (ديمورفوس) يتورم ويكتشف المئات من الصخور الأصغر حول زوج الكويكب وسيدرس الفريق هذه السمات لتحسين فهم التصادم وقياس خصائص كلتا الهيئتين.

ويستند البحث إلى القدرة المثبتة على تغيير مدار الكويكب. ومن شأن ذلك أن يساعد العلماء على تصميم أساليب أكثر موثوقية لحماية الأرض من تهديدات الكويكبات في المستقبل، وإن كان النجاح في نزعها يتوقف على الكويكب الخاص والوقت الكافي للإنذار.

eea11e7f-6000-48e9-ab70-49116ececcc2.original_title: Hera discovers the crater left by humanity’s first asteroid deflection test
eea11e7f-6000-48e9-ab70-49116ececcc2.original_summary: ESA’s new observations of Dimorphos show how a deliberate spacecraft collision changed the asteroid, advancing research on planetary defence.
eea11e7f-6000-48e9-ab70-49116ececcc2.original_body:
On 25 November 2026, the European Space Agency presented new observations from its Hera mission. The spacecraft is examining Dimorphos, the small asteroid whose orbit was deliberately changed by NASA’s DART mission in September 2022.

The new observations reveal a crater spanning much of the impacted side. Hera also found that Dimorphos is tumbling and detected hundreds of smaller rocks around the asteroid pair. The team will study these features to better understand the collision and measure the properties of both bodies.

The research builds on the demonstrated ability to alter an asteroid’s orbit. It could help scientists design more reliable methods to protect Earth from future asteroid threats, although successful deflection would depend on the particular asteroid and sufficient warning time.

Archive image: NASA/Johns Hopkins APL photographed Dimorphos during DART’s approach on 26 September 2022, before the collision. It shows the actual asteroid, not the newly observed crater.

9ea4e9c4-97bf-419f-ace5-9310fdc14031.original_title: Teenager returns to school after pioneering UK sickle cell treatment
9ea4e9c4-97bf-419f-ace5-9310fdc14031.original_summary: A 15-year-old girl treated with gene-edited stem cells in Manchester is back at school and has stopped experiencing sickle cell crises, her hospital reports.
9ea4e9c4-97bf-419f-ace5-9310fdc14031.original_body:
On 23 October, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust reported that Aisha, aged 15, had completed a course of Casgevy gene-editing treatment. Previously, severe sickle cell crises had repeatedly brought her to hospital and disrupted her education.

The treatment uses the patient’s own blood stem cells, modified outside the body and returned after preparatory chemotherapy. Aisha was discharged on 29 June 2026. She has since resumed school and become a prefect. Her hospital says she is no longer experiencing sickle cell crises, although she is receiving care for lingering muscle pain.

Her experience shows what this treatment can mean for an individual patient. It is a demanding procedure requiring specialist care, and this outcome should not be interpreted as a guarantee of success for everyone with sickle cell disease.

861bf328-afe4-419d-ad87-44494d113fe5.original_title: Two male cheetahs are released into Pilanesberg National Park
861bf328-afe4-419d-ad87-44494d113fe5.original_summary: Two male cheetahs moved safely from Madikwe to Pilanesberg, where they were released on 13 October 2026. Their arrival brings adult males back to a park that had two resident females.
861bf328-afe4-419d-ad87-44494d113fe5.original_body:
Two adult male cheetahs are exploring Pilanesberg National Park in South Africa after a carefully managed transfer from Madikwe Game Reserve. Their release on 13 October 2026 completed a conservation operation designed to strengthen the park's small cheetah population.

Before the move, Pilanesberg had two resident female cheetahs but no resident males. The Endangered Wildlife Trust coordinated the transfer through its Cheetah Conservation Project, working with veterinarians and staff at both protected areas. The animals received health checks and tracking collars, and spent time in a temporary enclosure after arrival.

The trust reported the move on 7 November. It is part of a broader programme that transfers cheetahs between South African reserves to maintain genetic diversity. Both males were released and began exploring their new surroundings. Whether they eventually breed with the resident females remains an outcome to watch, not a result already achieved.
